security_audit.summary: The reported matches are Markdown formatting, product documentation, or examples for optional Nimply connector setup. No evidence was found of shell execution, reconnaissance, or an attempt to override this audit. Connected workspace guidance can treat a supplied time as permission to schedule a post and requires cost disclosure without explicit consent to spend credits.

remediation.issue: A supplied time can be treated as permission to schedule a post.
remediation.suggestion: Keep timed proposals as drafts. Require clear authorization to schedule or publish, and verify the post, channels, time, and time zone before execution.

remediation.issue: The operating rules disclose credit costs without requiring authorization to spend credits.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit authorization or a user-approved credit budget before any billable design, agent run, or automation test. Pause if the estimate exceeds that budget.

semantic_findings.title: A Time Can Be Mistaken for Permission to Schedule
semantic_findings.description: The operating rules allow non-draft creation when a user supplies a time, even without requesting scheduling. A workspace with publish permissions could schedule a post the user meant to review first.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both operating guides explicitly list a supplied time as an alternative to a publish request. Actual scheduling depends on the connected workspace's permissions and approval settings.

semantic_findings.title: Credit Disclosure Does Not Require Spending Consent
semantic_findings.description: The rules require an estimate before running designs or agents but do not require the user to accept it. The automation test instructions also permit testing before approval and note that tests may consume credits.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly require disclosure but reserve user agreement for automation activation. The test guidance states that even a preview may use credits.

content.user_title: Plan Social Media Workflows With Nimply
content.value_statement: Social media teams need to choose agents, channels, and approvals without buying features they cannot use. This skill turns those requirements into a Nimply setup, credit estimate, and rollout plan.
actual_capabilities: Map publishing, inbox, and automation features to supported channels.
Recommend agents and approval steps for a specific business need.
Compare plan requirements and estimate monthly AI credits from expected usage.
Outline integrations using the REST API, MCP, lead webhooks, or no-code tools.
Use connected MCP tools to list workspace channels and create post drafts within granted permissions.
limitations: The skill works from a dated snapshot. Verify current prices, plan limits, and channel support before relying on it.
Workspace operations require a configured Nimply MCP connection and permissions for the selected workspace.
The API and MCP cannot directly read or send inbox messages. Lead webhooks deliver lead details, not conversations.
Activating Comment-to-DM or automatic inbox replies requires the Nimply app.

use_cases.title: Handle Routine Cafe Questions
use_cases.description: Choose an inbox agent in suggest mode and identify the business details it needs to draft replies about hours and menus.

use_cases.title: Plan Client Content Approvals
use_cases.description: Design a workflow that keeps client workspaces separate and gives each client a review step before posts are scheduled.

use_cases.title: Sync Leads to a CRM
use_cases.description: Plan a lead webhook integration with one credential per workspace, signature verification, deduplication, and only the lead fields your CRM needs.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Planner and Inbox
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the difference between Nimply Planner and Inbox for a small shop. Tell me what I can evaluate without connecting an account.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Inbox Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: My cafe receives 120 Instagram questions each month about menus and hours. Recommend one agent in suggest mode and estimate the monthly credits using a range.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Choose a setup and estimate costs

prompt_templates.title: Design an Agency Approval Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan approvals for three clients with separate Nimply workspaces. Cover roles, review steps, and failed post alerts. Do not make workspace changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Define a workflow for multiple clients

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Lead Webhook Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Nimply lead webhook integration for two client workspaces. Cover permissions, signature verification, deduplication, and which contact fields the CRM should store. Do not register endpoints.

output_examples.input: How should my cafe handle Instagram questions about our menu and hours?
output: Start with Restaurant Concierge in suggest mode on an Instagram professional account.
Add your menu and hours to the Business Profile. Have a teammate review suggested replies before sending them.
Send allergy questions to a person. Check current plan and credit costs before enabling the agent.

output_examples.input: Can I send new and updated lead stages to our CRM without accessing Nimply Inbox?
output: Use the lead created and lead stage changed webhooks. They send lead details, not inbox conversations.
Verify signatures, deduplicate by event ID, and acknowledge verified deliveries before doing slow CRM work.
Keep credentials separate for each workspace and store only the lead fields your CRM needs.

best_practices: Verify current plan limits, credit estimates, and channel support before selecting a setup.
Start with one agent in suggest mode and review its output before enabling automatic actions.
Use the minimum workspace permissions and confirm the target, action, and any credit cost before making changes.
anti_patterns: Assuming that every connected social channel supports direct messages or Comment-to-DM.
Treating a time in a draft brief as permission to schedule or publish a post.
Starting a credit-consuming job because the estimate was shown, without user authorization.

faq.question: Do I need a Nimply account to use this skill?
faq.answer: No account is needed for advice based on the bundled references. Live workspace actions require a connected, authorized Nimply workspace.

faq.question: Can the skill schedule or publish posts?
faq.answer: Connected MCP tools can schedule or publish when permissions and workspace approvals allow it. Ask for drafts if you only want to review the posts.

faq.question: Are agents included in the free plan?
faq.answer: The bundled references say agents require a paid plan or active trial. Check current pricing and credit allowances before selecting a plan.

faq.question: Can the connector read or send inbox messages?
faq.answer: No. The API and MCP do not directly read or send inbox messages. Lead webhooks provide lead details, not the underlying conversations.

faq.question: Where does Comment-to-DM work?
faq.answer: The bundled references list Instagram professional accounts and Facebook Pages. An owner or admin must activate it in the Nimply app.

faq.question: Which credentials should I use for multiple clients?
faq.answer: Use a separate credential for each workspace. Give each credential only the permissions its integration needs.
